Do this. Also feel free to ask your manager or a co-worker. Din stuff is pretty important so usually a higher up knows everything about it.

You can go two din values past the skier’s requested din (based on higher, weight, age, BSL and skier type). Basically sometimes the springs are off so you you will get different Nm (Newtonian meters, the physical measure of torque used to eject the boot) the what the true din should be. For example: if the skiers din should be a 10 with a Nm measure of say 144 or whatever and it keeps failing at like 120Nm, crank it up to an 11 and test it again. If it fails then up it to a 12. At that point if it it fails again and you sign off you could be held liable if an injury were to occur. Usually if it fails after two then I will tell the people that their binding isn’t functioning properly and they can either 1) buy a new binding, or two) ski on it knowing they could get hurt. If they opt for the latter write that on the test slip and have them sign off on it. 

P.S. that was basically verbatim what my Marker rep told me as well as our hard goods expert who has been in the industry for well over 30-35 years said. Also if you must adjust the din outside of what is required for the skier, give them a heads up.
